units.text: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system answers a question in two stages: it first retrieves passages from a document collection, then asks a language model to write an answer from those passages.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Why retrieval decides the answer

units.text: The model never sees the rest of the collection, so the answer can only be as good as the passages that retrieval hands it.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Why retrieval decides the answer

units.text: This note describes the retrieval design of the Harbor support assistant, an internal tool that answers questions over about 40,000 help-centre articles and release notes.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Why retrieval decides the answer

units.text: Keyword retrieval scores a passage by the query terms it contains, weighted so that rare terms count for more than common ones.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Keyword retrieval with BM25

units.text: BM25 is the usual scoring function for this; it also dampens the effect of a term repeated many times and corrects for passage length.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Keyword retrieval with BM25

units.text: BM25 needs no training and is cheap to run, which is why it remains the baseline.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Keyword retrieval with BM25

units.text: Its strength is exact matching.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Keyword retrieval with BM25

units.text: A query for the error code `E-4012` or the setting `sync.retry_window` finds the passages that contain those strings, even when they appear only once in the whole collection.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Keyword retrieval with BM25

units.text: Its weakness is vocabulary mismatch: a user who asks "why does my upload stall" will not match a passage that only says "transfers pause when the connection drops".
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Keyword retrieval with BM25

units.text: Vector retrieval turns the query and every passage into embeddings, lists of numbers produced by an encoder model, and returns the passages whose embeddings lie closest to the query's.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Vector retrieval with embeddings

units.text: Passages that mean the same thing end up close together even when they share no words, so the stalled-upload question can find the passage about paused transfers.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Vector retrieval with embeddings

units.text: Embeddings are weaker on exact codes and identifiers.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Vector retrieval with embeddings

units.text: To the encoder, `E-4012` and `E-4021` look almost the same, and a rare product name may be split into fragments that carry little meaning.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Vector retrieval with embeddings

units.text: In our tests, vector retrieval alone missed the correct passage for 31 of 50 queries that consisted mainly of an error code.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Vector retrieval with embeddings

units.text: Embeddings must also be recomputed whenever the encoder changes, which for this collection takes about 6 hours.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Vector retrieval with embeddings

units.text: Hybrid search runs both retrievers on the same query and merges their result lists.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: Hybrid search can improve recall when lexical and semantic signals are complementary, that is, when each retriever finds relevant passages that the other misses.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: If both retrievers tend to return the same passages, or if one of them is poorly tuned for the collection, merging adds latency without adding much.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: BM25 scores and vector similarities sit on different scales, so they cannot simply be added together.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: We use Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), which ignores the raw scores and uses only the rank of each passage in each list.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: A passage receives `1/(k + rank)` from every list it appears in, and the contributions are summed.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: We set `k = 60`, a common default; a larger k flattens the difference between the top ranks and the lower ones.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Combining the two signals

units.text: Each retriever returns its top 50 passages, so the fused list holds at most 100 candidates, and usually fewer because some passages appear in both lists.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Candidate generation

units.text: This stage is tuned for recall rather than precision: the goal is to make sure the right passage is somewhere in the list, not that it comes first.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Candidate generation

units.text: Raising the limit to 100 per retriever put the right passage in the list slightly more often, but it roughly doubled the time spent reranking, so we kept 50.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Candidate generation

units.text: A reranker then rescores the fused candidates.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: We use a cross-encoder, a model that reads the query and one passage together and outputs a single relevance score.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: Because it sees both texts at once, it judges relevance far more accurately than either retriever.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: That accuracy is expensive, so the cross-encoder runs only on the fused candidates, never on the whole collection.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: After reranking we keep the top 8 passages.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: Reranking improves the precision of the top results, but it does not guarantee that the final answer is correct.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: The reranker can only reorder what retrieval found: if the right passage is not among the candidates, reranking cannot recover it.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: A passage can also be highly relevant and still out of date, which no relevance score will detect.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Reranking

units.text: The language model receives the question and the top 8 passages, and is instructed to answer only from them and to cite the passages it used.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Generation

units.text: If none of the passages addresses the question, it should say so rather than answer from its general knowledge.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Generation

units.text: Citations let a reader check each claim against its passage, but they do not show whether the passage itself is current.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Generation

units.text: For example, asked "What does E-4012 mean?", the assistant retrieves the error-code table through BM25 and the article on resumable uploads through vector search, and the reranker keeps both in the top 8, so the answer can define the code and explain the fix.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Generation

units.text: Every stage buys relevance with time or money.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: On an internal test set of 400 questions, we measured:
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Configuration | Correct passage in top 8 | Median latency | Cost per 1,000 queries
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost
Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Vector only | 68% | 60 ms | $0.10
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Hybrid (RRF) | 79% | 70 ms | $0.12
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Hybrid + reranker | 88% | 190 ms | $0.95
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Reranking adds about 120 ms per query, most of it spent running the cross-encoder over up to 100 candidates, and it accounts for most of the cost increase.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: These figures come from one collection and one query set; a collection with fewer exact identifiers may see a smaller gain from BM25, and a different reranker will have a different latency.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Teams with a strict latency budget can rerank fewer candidates, for example the top 30 of the fused list instead of all of them, at some cost in recall.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Relevance, latency and cost

units.text: Hybrid search widens the net, reranking sorts the catch, and generation can only work with the passages it is given.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Summary

units.text: Each step helps only under its own conditions, and none of them makes the final answer certain to be right.
units.topic: Hybrid search and reranking in the Harbor assistant › Summary
